newsitem.title: USA: CBOT WHEAT ENDS UP ON EXPORTS, CWB WHEAT ESTIMATE.
newsitem.headline: CBOT WHEAT ENDS UP ON EXPORTS, CWB WHEAT ESTIMATE.

text.p: CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed higher on export news and news the Canadian Wheat Board sharply cut its estimate for Canadian wheat production, traders said.
"The wheat market held together because the Canadian Wheat Board cut their crop," said Marty Colgan, of Chicago-based trade house LFG Futures.
The Canadian Wheat Board Thursday said it was forecasting wheat output in western Canada this year of 21.6 million tonnes, below the 29.5 million produced last year.
Also USDA's weekly export sales report Thursday pegged U.S. net export sales of wheat for the 1997-98 (June-May) marketing year at 765,100 tonnes, above expectations for 650,000 to 750,000 tonnes.
Also there was talk Egypt by this weekend would be in the market for 300,000 to 400,000 tonnes of wheat.
Wheat closed two cents higher to two lower, with September up one at $3.63-1/4.

Gains were limited by a drop in corn and soybean futures plus rain in Australia's dry wheat region. News the EU has accepted export bids for 472,000 tonnes of soft wheat grain at an export tax of three Ecus per tonne also capped gains.
But the EU overnight also increased to six Ecus from the previous three Ecus its tax on wheat exports, a scenario viewed as mildly supportive for U.S. wheat futures.

In spread dealings, FIMAT Futures did 1.5 million bushels of December/September at 15-1/2 cents, premium December and E.D. and F. Man International spread one million September/December at 15-1/4 cents, premium December, traders said.
Cargill Inc bought 2.5 million bushels of December, Continental Grain bought 1.5 million bushels of September and FIMAT Futures bought four million bushels of December, traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 24,000 contracts, above the 22,715 traded Wednesday.

In wheat options, Continental Grain bought 400 December $3.80 puts at 22 cents, bought 400 December $3.80 calls at 17 cents, sold 400 December $3.50 puts at eight cents and sold 400 December $4.30 calls at 4-1/8 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 8,000 contracts, above the 5,439 traded Wednesday.
